title: Early abort coalescing and resumable prefix preservation
creator: Ariel Nunez
description: Problem summary: frequent client disconnects and aggressive client-side retries cause lots of small, overlapping partial generations and repeated GC/compaction work on the prefix cache. This increases CPU/GPU scheduling churn and raises p99 tail latency for other in-flight streams. We need a mechanism to reduce churn by coalescing rapid early-aborts and preserve a compact, resumable prefix so clients can resume without forcing full re-generation.
background: Current behavior: when a client disconnects mid-generation we create an ephemeral partial blob and schedule fast-path eviction. Many clients (mobile SDKs, flaky networks) reconnect within 100-500ms and trigger a new generation; the system ends up compacting the same prefix multiple times. Existing mitigations (short grace periods, soft-drop) reduce some churn but don't preserve a safe, compacted resumable prefix tied to a resume token. This ticket proposes a coordinated approach: early-abort coalescing window + compacted prefix preservation with resume-token-safe checksums and a compatibility shim for older SDKs.
proposed_solution: 1) Early-abort coalescing: introduce an abort-coalesce window (configurable default 250ms) per (customer, model-variant, shard). On first abort create a lightweight sentinel entry with expiration = now + coalesce_window. Subsequent aborts in window bump a counter but do not trigger individual compaction/Garbage Collection. After window expires, a single compaction job runs that either preserves a resumable compact prefix (if any valid prefix exists) or performs normal eviction.
proposed_solution_2: 2) Resumable prefix preservation: when compaction runs we produce a compacted-prefix artifact and compute a 64-bit checksum + HMAC-like bound (compacted_prefix_crc). The resume token returned to clients includes (prefix_id, compacted_prefix_crc, generation_epoch). On resume the server verifies checksum to avoid mismatched KV cache state across restarts. The preserved compacted-prefix is stored with a short retention TTL (configurable, default 10m) and is eligible for reclaim if not resumed.
compatibility_and_shim: To support older SDKs that do not set resume headers, add an opt-in compatibility header X-Rdwd-Resume-V1. When present, servers accept legacy resume semantics that attempt a best-effort match by sequence-id and fall back if checksum absent. This is behind a feature flag and defaults to disabled for enterprise where strict auditability is required.
function_call_and_structured_output_cons: Function/tool-call boundaries are treated as atomic in prefix preservation: if the compacted prefix ends inside a pending tool invocation we mark the resume token as 'function_boundary_pending' and require the client SDK to either (a) re-issue the tool call with the saved arguments or (b) accept that the tool call will be re-executed. For structured JSON outputs we maintain an end-of-structure marker in the compacted artifact to avoid resuming into syntactically invalid state.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Longer coalesce windows reduce churn but increase time until orphaned storage reclaimed (tunable per-customer).
- Preserving compacted prefix increases short-term storage and adds checksum verification complexity.
- Function-call re-execution risk: re-running tool invocations can have side effects; we will default to conservative behavior (require SDK explicit resume consent for tool re-execution) and surface developer docs.
- Complexity of resume verification may require migration of existing resume tokens; we will support backward compatibility via feature-flagged grace period.
acceptance_criteria:
- Single compaction job per coalesce-window for bursty aborts in local load tests.
- Measured reduction of compaction runs by >= 40% under flaky-client workload in benchmark harness.
- Resume succeeds with matching compacted_prefix_crc for >= 99.9% of resumed sessions during canary.
- No increase in p50/p90 latency for steady-state generations.
- Integration tests for function-call boundary preservation and structured-output resume pass in CI.
implementation_notes:
- Add abort_sentinal table keyed by (customer_id, model_variant, shard_id) with fields: first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts, abort_count, scheduled_compaction_ts, compacted_prefix_id.
- Extend prefix artifact metadata with compacted_prefix_crc (string) and function_boundary_flag (boolean).
- Add server-side resume verification step that checks compacted_prefix_crc and generation_epoch before accepting client resume.
- Expose new SDK API: ResumeOptions { allow_tool_reexec: bool, compatibility_header: bool } and document semantics.
- Feature flag: 'early_abort_coalesce_v1' default off; rollout via gradual canary.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for sentinel lifecycle, compaction scheduling, and checksum generation.
- Integration tests: simulate 1000 clients with 10% disconnect frequency; verify compaction counts and resume success.
- Chaos test: introduce network flaps between client and server at 50ms-1s intervals and confirm system stability.
- Regression test for function-calls: replay tool-invocation sequences and assert either idempotent re-execution or explicit SDK consent flow.
- Performance benchmark: compare GC/compaction CPU and p99 latency before/after under controlled load.
metrics_and_alerts:
Primary metrics to track:
- compaction_jobs_per_minute (expected drop)
- orphaned_prefix_storage_bytes
- resume_success_rate (by compacted_prefix_crc match)
- average_abort_coalesce_window_utilization
- user_reported_resume_failures (dashboard and pager alarm if > 0.1% over 30m)
Set an alert if resume_success_rate < 99.7% for 15m during rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged server build + SDK changes in a dev build.
2) Canary to 5% traffic (non-enterprise tenants) for 48h, monitor metrics and logs.
3) Expand to 20% for 72h with tighter monitoring.
4) Enable enterprise opt-in via console flags after 2 successful canary waves.
5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stability.
Rollback: flip feature flag off; compacted artifacts remain but resume tokens are ignored until re-enabled.
open_questions:
- Default coalesce window: 250ms vs 500ms tradeoffs for mobile clients?
- How to present tool-reexec consent in SDK UI for higher-level framework integrations?
- Retention TTL: default 10m ok for cross-region resume use-cases?
- Should we provide a manual admin endpoint to force-preserve a compacted prefix for troubleshooting?
